headline: Chips and Optical Names Lead a Lopsided Friday Session
body_html:
Friday's midday tape is decidedly mixed, with decliners outpacing advancers 334 to 206 across the universe. Semiconductors stand as the lone sector in positive territory with a gain of roughly 1.1%, while every other major group trades in the red. Software and Materials trail the pack, each down more than 0.6%, leaving the broader market without meaningful upside participation heading into the afternoon.

The session's standout mover is Coherent, the optical-networking specialist, up 3.75% and pacing all gainers. Corning is also drawing attention with a 3% advance, suggesting investor appetite for connectivity-infrastructure names tied to data-transport buildout. On the industrial side, Forgent Power Solutions and ABB Ltd each added more than 3%, offering a rare bright spot in an otherwise defensive posture across cyclicals.

The sharpest selling has landed in metallurgical coal, where Alpha Metallurgical Resources shed 5.58% and Warrior Met Coal fell 4.33% — together dragging the Materials sector. Nucor's 3.39% decline piles additional pressure on steel-adjacent names. With geopolitical tension around the Strait of Hormuz still front of mind and oil prices easing modestly on diminished supply-disruption fears, traders will watch energy and materials into the close for any late-session capitulation or relief bounce.

briefs.headline: Metallurgical Coal Names Bear the Brunt of Friday Selling
briefs.body: Alpha Metallurgical Resources and Warrior Met Coal are the session's two worst performers, off 5.58% and 4.33% respectively. The paired decline points to sector-specific pressure on met coal rather than a broad commodity selloff, though Nucor's concurrent 3.39% drop suggests steel-chain sentiment is uniformly sour heading into the weekend.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Strait Traffic Shows Tentative Signs of Normalizing
briefs.body: Vessel movements through the Strait of Hormuz have dipped below the 10-day average, yet LNG tankers have begun reappearing outside the strait — a cautious signal that some shipping interests may be testing the route again. The development comes even as the broader Iran conflict continues to weigh on jet-fuel financing costs and aviation-sector planning.

briefs.headline: Oil Slips as Saudi Supply-Disruption Concerns Recede
briefs.body: Crude prices edged lower through mid-session after market participants scaled back fears of a significant interruption to Saudi Arabian output. The modest relief in oil is contributing to a relatively contained energy-sector decline of 0.34%, though coal-related names have not shared in that reprieve, falling sharply on their own fundamental pressures.

briefs.headline: China Posts Record Jet-Fuel Exports Despite Regional Conflict
briefs.body: China's refined-fuel export volumes for August surpassed pre-Iran-war levels, with jet-fuel shipments reaching a record high, according to fresh trade data. The figures suggest Beijing's refiners are capitalizing on supply gaps left by the conflict, redirecting product to international markets at an accelerated pace.

briefs.headline: Trump Set for Contentious UN General Assembly Appearance
briefs.body: With the Iran conflict still unresolved, President Trump is expected to face pointed skepticism from world leaders when he addresses the United Nations General Assembly. U.S. officials separately confirmed that Iranian leadership will be permitted to attend the gathering, setting the stage for charged diplomatic optics on the margins of the session.

briefs.headline: Kremlin Moves to Seize Control of Nestlé's Russian Operations
briefs.body: Russia's government has escalated pressure on Western corporate assets by targeting Nestlé's business presence in the country, part of a broader pattern of the Kremlin tightening its grip on foreign-owned enterprises that remained after the wave of post-2022 Western corporate exits. The move renews concerns among multinationals still weighing exposure to Russian-domiciled assets.
